name: pdfjs-dist in jevsume
what_it_is: The prebuilt npm distribution of Mozilla PDF.js. Jevsume already uses its display API for PDF text extraction and its packaged module worker through a Vite URL import.
render_model: Currently text extraction only in jevsume; the installed API can add Canvas page rendering with PDFPageProxy.render, a DOM TextLayer, and an optional DOM/SVG AnnotationLayer.
annotation_support: Current jevsume code has no annotation UI. Recommended extension is overlay-only application annotations in a separate SVG; optionally render PDF.js AnnotationLayer for existing PDF links/forms/annotations, without writing jevsume state into PDF dictionaries.
coordinate_space: Use each PDFPageProxy's unscaled PDF page coordinates as persisted geometry and one PageViewport per render scale to derive canvas/CSS positions. Version 6.3.289 lacks convertToViewportRectangle; call convertToViewportPoint for both corners and normalize bounds.
desktop_fit: Strong: the dependency and worker setup already exist, so a custom React page component needs page.render lifecycle, viewport sizing, layer containers, and cancellation rather than a second PDF SDK.
mobile_fit: Good [uncertain]: responsive viewport scaling uses the same APIs, but this task did not benchmark large resumes or verify touch/pinch interaction on target devices.
overlay_chat_fit: Strong: preserve PDF page coordinates for anchors and render boxes, pins, selected states, and chat triggers in an SVG sibling layer sharing the active PageViewport.
license: Apache License 2.0, inherited from Mozilla PDF.js.
already_in_repo: Yes: package.json declares ^6.3.289. src/lib/extract.ts imports pdfjs-dist and pdf.worker.min.mjs?url, assigns GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc, loads ArrayBuffer data, calls getPage/getTextContent, and joins TextItem.str values.
risks: The caret permits upgrades with API-minor changes; flattening items with inserted spaces loses exact page/item offset correspondence; layers require matching CSS; React rerenders must cancel stale RenderTasks; native AnnotationLayer behavior should not be confused with jevsume's application overlay.
recommendation: use — pin or deliberately test the 6.3 API during implementation, reuse the existing worker configuration, add canvas and structured text-content paths, and persist custom overlay state outside the PDF.
uncertain: The lockfile-resolved installed version was not inspected because dependencies were not present in node_modules during this research; package.json requests ^6.3.289 and npm identifies 6.3.289 as the current package version.
Mobile render-memory and gesture performance require separate empirical validation.
The span-to-glyph task must determine robust matching between flattened Jev text and page TextItems.
